s161.content:
Timothy, the son of a Greek father and a Jewish mother, learned the faith from his mother Eunice and grandmother Lois. He became St. Paul’s closest companion, traveled with him on his missions, and was trusted with difficult assignments in Corinth and Thessalonica.

Two of Paul’s letters are addressed to him as the leader of the church in Ephesus. Tradition says he was martyred there for opposing a pagan festival. He shares his feast with St. Titus.
s161.intercession: St. Timothy, faithful companion of St. Paul, pray for us. Strengthen young leaders in the Church, and help us to guard the faith we have received. Amen.

s162.content:
Martha of Bethany, sister of Mary and Lazarus, welcomed Jesus into her home as a dear friend. When she complained that her sister left her to serve alone, Jesus gently reminded her of the "one thing" needful.

Yet it was Martha who, at her brother’s tomb, made one of the great professions of faith in the Gospels: that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God. She is the patron of cooks, servers, and all who offer hospitality.
s162.intercession: St. Martha, who served the Lord in your home, pray for us. Help us to work without anxiety, to welcome others generously, and to never forget the one thing needful. Amen.

s163.content:
Clement was one of the earliest bishops of Rome, counted by St. Irenaeus as the third successor of St. Peter. Around the year 96 he wrote a letter to the church in Corinth, urging an end to a rebellion against its presbyters.

His letter is one of the oldest Christian writings outside the New Testament and an early witness to the authority of the Roman church. Tradition says he was exiled and martyred by drowning with an anchor tied to his neck.
s163.intercession: Pope St. Clement, pray for us. Help us to keep peace and good order in the Church, and to love the unity that Christ desires. Amen.

s164.content:
By tradition, Cosmas and Damian were twin brothers from Arabia who practiced medicine in Syria without ever charging their patients, winning many to Christ through their generosity. They became known in the East as the "Unmercenaries."

They were arrested during the persecution of Diocletian and beheaded. Their names are recalled in the Roman Canon of the Mass, and they are patrons of physicians, surgeons, and pharmacists.
s164.intercession: Sts. Cosmas and Damian, who healed freely for love of Christ, pray for us. Bless all who care for the sick, and grant healing to those who suffer. Amen.

s165.content:
According to tradition, Catherine was a brilliant young noblewoman of Alexandria who rebuked the emperor for persecuting Christians. He summoned fifty philosophers to debate her, and she won them all to the faith.

Condemned to be broken on a spiked wheel, she was saved when the wheel shattered at her touch, and was then beheaded. One of the voices St. Joan of Arc heard, she is the patron of philosophers, students, and young women.
s165.intercession: St. Catherine of Alexandria, wise and courageous witness, pray for us. Help students and scholars to seek the truth and to defend it with grace. Amen.

s166.content:
Pancras was an orphan from Phrygia who came to Rome with his uncle and was baptized there. When the persecution of Diocletian began, he refused to sacrifice to the gods and was beheaded at about fourteen years old.

His tomb on the Via Aurelia became a place of pilgrimage, and St. Augustine of Canterbury dedicated one of England’s first churches to him. He is a patron of children and of those who keep their promises.
s166.intercession: St. Pancras, young and fearless martyr, pray for us. Give children and young people the courage to stand firm in their faith. Amen.

s167.content:
Florian was a Roman army officer in the province of Noricum, in present-day Austria. When ordered to round up Christians during the persecution of Diocletian, he declared his own faith instead.

He was scourged and drowned in the river Enns with a stone around his neck. A legend that he saved a burning town with a single bucket of water made him the patron of firefighters, chimney sweeps, and all in danger from fire.
s167.intercession: St. Florian, pray for us. Protect firefighters and all who rush into danger to save others, and keep our homes safe from fire. Amen.

s168.content:
By tradition, Maurice was an Egyptian Christian who commanded the Theban Legion, a Roman unit raised in Upper Egypt. Stationed in the Alps, the legion refused to kill innocent Christians or to sacrifice to the gods.

The emperor had the legion executed for their refusal. The abbey of Saint-Maurice in Switzerland has honored him since the 6th century, and he is a patron of soldiers, swordsmiths, and infantrymen.
s168.intercession: St. Maurice, soldier of Christ, pray for us. Help all who serve in the armed forces to remain faithful to God and to refuse every unjust command. Amen.

s169.content:
Januarius (San Gennaro) was bishop of Benevento in southern Italy. During the persecution of Diocletian he visited imprisoned Christians, was arrested himself, and was beheaded near Pozzuoli.

He is the patron of Naples, where a vial said to contain his dried blood is kept in the cathedral. On his feast and a few other days each year, the people gather to pray for the blood to liquefy, a phenomenon recorded since 1389.
s169.intercession: St. Januarius, faithful bishop and martyr, pray for us. Protect the people of Naples and all who call on you, and strengthen the shepherds of the Church. Amen.

s170.content:
Apollonia was an elderly consecrated virgin of Alexandria, killed during a riot against Christians in 249. Her story is told in a letter by the local bishop, St. Dionysius, quoted by the historian Eusebius.

The mob broke out her teeth and threatened to burn her alive unless she denied Christ. Rather than give them the chance, she walked into the fire herself. She is the patron of dentists and those with toothache.
s170.intercession: St. Apollonia, who held fast to Christ through great suffering, pray for us. Bring relief to all in pain, and bless those who care for them. Amen.

s171.content:
Denis was sent from Rome to evangelize Gaul and became the first bishop of Paris. His preaching won so many converts that he was arrested with two companions, Rusticus and Eleutherius, and beheaded on the hill now called Montmartre, "the mountain of the martyr."

A legend tells that he carried his own head to the place of his burial. The abbey of Saint-Denis grew over his tomb, and he is a patron of France and of Paris.
s171.intercession: St. Denis, first bishop of Paris, pray for us. Help us to carry the Gospel boldly, even at great cost. Amen.

s172.content:
Hilary was a married pagan scholar who found his way to Christianity through reading Scripture, and was later chosen bishop of Poitiers in Gaul. He became the leading Western defender of Christ’s divinity against Arianism, earning the name "the Athanasius of the West."

Exiled to Asia Minor for his stand, he used the time to study Greek theology and write his great work On the Trinity. He was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1851.
s172.intercession: St. Hilary, steadfast defender of the faith, pray for us. Help us to know and love the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and to profess the truth with courage. Amen.

s173.content:
Cyril was bishop of Jerusalem during the fierce controversies over Arianism and was driven into exile three times. He is best remembered for his Catechetical Lectures, delivered to those preparing for Baptism at Easter.

The lectures explain the Creed and the sacraments with remarkable clarity, and offer a vivid picture of the liturgy in 4th-century Jerusalem, including the Real Presence of Christ in the Eucharist. He was named a Doctor of the Church in 1882.
s173.intercession: St. Cyril of Jerusalem, pray for us. Bless all who teach the faith and all who are preparing to enter the Church. Amen.

s174.content:
The younger brother of St. Basil the Great and St. Macrina, Gregory was a married teacher of rhetoric before becoming bishop of Nyssa. He was one of the three "Cappadocian Fathers" who shaped the Church’s language about the Trinity at the Council of Constantinople in 381.

His Life of Moses describes the spiritual life as an endless ascent into God, always growing, never finished. He is honored as one of the great mystical theologians of the East.
s174.intercession: St. Gregory of Nyssa, pray for us. Draw us ever deeper into the mystery of God, that we may never stop growing in love. Amen.

s175.content:
Macrina was the eldest of ten children in a remarkable family of saints that included St. Basil the Great and St. Gregory of Nyssa. After her fiancé died, she turned the family estate into a community of prayer where former servants and noblewomen lived as equals.

Gregory called her "the Teacher," and his Life of Macrina records her deathbed conversation on the soul and the resurrection. Her example helped shape Eastern monasticism.
s175.intercession: St. Macrina, wise teacher of your family, pray for us. Make our homes into places of prayer, and help us to lead our loved ones to God. Amen.

s176.content:
Moses was an Ethiopian slave in Egypt who became the violent leader of a band of robbers. While hiding from the law among the monks of the desert of Scetis, he was moved by their peace and humility, and asked to become one of them.

He became a much-loved abbot known for his gentleness. Asked to judge a brother, he came carrying a leaking basket of sand: "My sins run out behind me, and I do not see them." He was killed by raiders at about seventy-five.
s176.intercession: St. Moses the Black, transformed by God’s mercy, pray for us. Help all who struggle with violence and addiction to find peace in Christ. Amen.

s177.content:
Paula was a wealthy Roman noblewoman and mother of five. After the death of her husband she devoted herself to prayer and the study of Scripture under St. Jerome, learning Hebrew so well that she could chant the psalms in the original.

She followed Jerome to Bethlehem, where she founded monasteries for men and women and a hostel for pilgrims, spending her entire fortune on the poor. She helped Jerome with his translation of the Bible.
s177.intercession: St. Paula, pray for us. Give widows comfort and strength, and help us to love the Scriptures and to share our goods with the poor. Amen.

s178.content:
Peter was archbishop of Ravenna, then the capital of the Western Roman Empire. His sermons, short, warm, and full of images, earned him the name "Chrysologus," meaning "golden word."

About 180 of his sermons survive, many on the Incarnation, the Creed, and the Lord’s Prayer. He urged frequent reception of the Eucharist and loyalty to the bishop of Rome. Pope Benedict XIII declared him a Doctor of the Church in 1729.
s178.intercession: St. Peter Chrysologus, pray for us. Bless preachers with golden words, and open our hearts to receive the word of God. Amen.

s179.content:
Dewi Sant, the patron saint of Wales, founded a monastery at Mynyw (now St Davids) where his monks lived a strict life of manual labor, drinking only water and keeping long hours of prayer.

He traveled widely as a preacher and bishop. His last sermon is remembered in the words, "Be joyful, keep the faith, and do the little things." Welsh people wear daffodils or leeks on his feast day.
s179.intercession: St. David, pray for us. Teach us to be joyful, to keep the faith, and to do the little things well for the love of God. Amen.

s180.content:
Augustine was prior of a monastery in Rome when Pope St. Gregory the Great sent him with about forty monks to bring the Gospel to the Anglo-Saxons. They landed in Kent in 597, where Queen Bertha, already a Christian, helped them win a hearing.

King Æthelberht was baptized, along with thousands of his people, and Augustine became the first archbishop of Canterbury. He is called the "Apostle to the English."
s180.intercession: St. Augustine of Canterbury, pray for us. Bless all missionaries, and help us to bring the faith to those who have not yet heard it. Amen.

s181.content:
Columbanus was an Irish monk who left his homeland at about forty-five to become a "pilgrim for Christ" on the Continent. He founded monasteries at Annegray, Luxeuil, and Bobbio, which became centers of learning and holiness for centuries.

His strict rule and fearless rebukes of corrupt nobles made him powerful enemies, and he was exiled from Burgundy. He is often credited with helping to renew Christian life across early medieval Europe.
s181.intercession: St. Columbanus, pilgrim for Christ, pray for us. Give us courage to leave our comfort for the sake of the Gospel. Amen.

s182.content:
Hilda was a Northumbrian princess baptized at thirteen. She later became abbess of the double monastery of Whitby, where monks and nuns lived side by side, and where five future bishops were trained.

Kings and commoners came to her for advice. She hosted the Synod of Whitby in 664, and encouraged the cowherd Cædmon, the first known English poet, to set Scripture to verse. Her wisdom and kindness made her beloved throughout England.
s182.intercession: St. Hilda, wise abbess and teacher, pray for us. Bless all who educate the young, and help leaders to seek good counsel. Amen.

s183.content:
Cuthbert was a shepherd boy who saw a vision of angels and entered the monastery of Melrose. He became a tireless missionary to the remote villages of Northumbria, then prior of Lindisfarne.

He longed for solitude and lived for years as a hermit on the tiny island of Inner Farne, praying among the seabirds. Called reluctantly to be a bishop, he served two years before returning to die in his hermitage. His shrine is in Durham Cathedral.
s183.intercession: St. Cuthbert, lover of prayer and of God’s creatures, pray for us. Help us to find God in silence and to serve His people gladly. Amen.

s184.content:
John was born in Damascus under Muslim rule and served as a high official at the caliph’s court before becoming a monk at the monastery of Mar Saba near Jerusalem.

When the Byzantine emperor ordered the destruction of sacred images, John wrote powerful defenses of icons: since God became visible in Christ, He can be depicted. His Fountain of Knowledge summarized the theology of the Greek Fathers. He was named a Doctor of the Church in 1890.
s184.intercession: St. John Damascene, defender of holy images, pray for us. Help us to see in all beauty a reflection of the God who became man. Amen.

s185.content:
Stephen was the first king of Hungary, crowned in the year 1000 with a crown sent by the pope. He worked to convert his people, founded dioceses and monasteries, and built a Christian kingdom out of a nation of nomadic tribes.

He was known for his care for the poor, often distributing alms in disguise. His Admonitions to his son Emeric urged humility, mercy, and prayer. He and Emeric were canonized together in 1083.
s185.intercession: St. Stephen of Hungary, pray for us. Guide those who govern nations, that they may rule with justice, humility, and mercy. Amen.

s186.content:
Edward was the last king of the House of Wessex. After years of exile in Normandy, he ruled England for twenty-four years, during which he kept the kingdom largely at peace and became known for his piety and generosity to the poor.

He rebuilt Westminster Abbey, where he was buried shortly after its consecration. He was canonized in 1161 and was for centuries honored as a patron of England.
s186.intercession: St. Edward the Confessor, pray for us. Help leaders to seek peace, and help us to use our gifts for the glory of God and the good of the poor. Amen.

s187.content:
Orphaned and mistreated as a child, Peter was rescued by an older brother who saw to his education. He became a famous teacher, then left it all to become a hermit-monk at Fonte Avellana.

Popes repeatedly called him out of his cell to fight corruption in the Church, especially simony and clerical immorality, and he was made a cardinal against his wishes. His letters and sermons fueled the great reform of the 11th century. He was named a Doctor of the Church in 1828.
s187.intercession: St. Peter Damian, pray for us. Renew the Church in holiness, and give her leaders the courage to root out every corruption. Amen.

s188.content:
Hedwig was a Bavarian noblewoman married at twelve to Duke Henry of Silesia, with whom she had seven children. Together they founded hospitals and monasteries, including a Cistercian convent at Trebnitz.

She lived simply, walked barefoot even in winter, and cared personally for the poor and for lepers. After many family sorrows, including the death of her son in battle against the Mongols, she retired to Trebnitz as a widow. She is a patron of Silesia.
s188.intercession: St. Hedwig, pray for us. Comfort families in sorrow, and help us to use whatever we have in the service of the poor. Amen.

s189.content:
Ferdinand united the kingdoms of Castile and León and was known as a just ruler who cared for his people and was reluctant to burden them with taxes. A devoted husband and father of thirteen children, he was also a Franciscan tertiary.

He supported the young University of Salamanca, began the great cathedral of Burgos, and was buried in Seville Cathedral. He is a patron of engineers, rulers, and the poor.
s189.intercession: St. Ferdinand, pray for us. Grant to all who govern a love of justice and a care for the poor. Amen.

s190.content:
Raymond was a Catalan priest and brilliant scholar of law who joined the Dominicans in middle age. At the pope’s request he compiled the Decretals, the official collection of Church law that was used for nearly seven centuries.

He served as master general of the Dominicans, encouraged St. Thomas Aquinas to write the Summa contra Gentiles, and helped found the Mercedarian order to ransom captives. He lived to about one hundred. He is a patron of lawyers.
s190.intercession: St. Raymond, pray for us. Bless lawyers and judges with wisdom and honesty, and help all of us to love God’s law. Amen.

s191.content:
Gertrude was placed in the convent of Helfta in Saxony at five years old and grew into a gifted scholar. At twenty-five she experienced a profound conversion, turning from secular learning to Scripture and the love of Christ.

Her visions, recorded in The Herald of Divine Love, are among the earliest to describe devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus. She is the only woman saint called "the Great," and is a patron of the West Indies.
s191.intercession: St. Gertrude, pray for us. Draw us into the Heart of Jesus, and help us to trust in His tender love. Amen.

s192.content:
Vincent was a Spanish Dominican and one of the most famous preachers of the Middle Ages. For twenty years he traveled across Spain, France, Switzerland, and Italy, often preaching to thousands in the open air on repentance and the Last Judgment.

He worked to end the Great Western Schism, when rival claimants divided the papacy. Many miracles and conversions were attributed to him. He died in Brittany, where his tomb remains in Vannes Cathedral.
s192.intercession: St. Vincent Ferrer, pray for us. Stir our hearts to conversion, and help us to work for the unity of the Church. Amen.

s193.content:
As a young man, Bernardine nursed plague victims in Siena. He became a Franciscan friar and the greatest preacher in 15th-century Italy, drawing enormous crowds that filled the city squares for hours.

He spread devotion to the Holy Name of Jesus, holding up a tablet bearing the monogram IHS for the people to venerate. He reformed his order and refused three bishoprics. He is a patron of advertisers and public speakers.
s193.intercession: St. Bernardine, pray for us. Teach us to love and reverence the holy Name of Jesus, and bless all who speak in His name. Amen.

s194.content:
John was a lawyer and governor of Perugia who, after being imprisoned in a war, experienced a conversion and joined the Franciscans under St. Bernardine of Siena. He became a renowned preacher and papal envoy across Central Europe.

In 1456, at about seventy, he helped rally the Christian army that broke the Ottoman siege of Belgrade, leading troops himself. He died of plague weeks later. He is a patron of military chaplains and jurists.
s194.intercession: St. John of Capistrano, pray for us. Give courage to all who defend the innocent, and bless military chaplains in their ministry. Amen.

s195.content:
Casimir was a prince of Poland and Lithuania, the son of King Casimir IV. At thirteen he was sent to claim the throne of Hungary but soon withdrew, refusing to fight a war he considered unjust.

He lived a life of prayer and penance at court, wore simple clothing, and gave generously to the poor. He had a great devotion to Our Lady. He died of tuberculosis at twenty-five and is the patron saint of Lithuania.
s195.intercession: St. Casimir, pray for us. Help young people to choose holiness over power, and keep us faithful to Christ in every place. Amen.

s196.content:
Nicholas was a Swiss farmer, soldier, judge, and father of ten children. At fifty, with the consent of his wife Dorothea, he left home to live as a hermit in a nearby ravine, where he is said to have lived for nearly twenty years on the Eucharist alone.

People came from all over Europe for his counsel. In 1481 his advice prevented a civil war between the Swiss cantons. "Brother Klaus" is the patron saint of Switzerland.
s196.intercession: St. Nicholas of Flüe, peacemaker, pray for us. Bring peace to divided communities, and help families to support one another in following God’s call. Amen.

s197.content:
Angela was orphaned young in northern Italy and became a Franciscan tertiary. Seeing how many girls grew up without any instruction in the faith, she gathered women to teach them in their own homes.

In 1535 she founded the Company of St. Ursula, the first order of women dedicated to teaching. Its members at first lived consecrated lives in their own families. The Ursulines went on to found schools across Europe and the Americas.
s197.intercession: St. Angela Merici, pray for us. Bless all teachers, especially those who form young women in faith and knowledge. Amen.

s198.content:
John was a Portuguese shepherd, soldier, and bookseller who underwent a dramatic conversion after hearing St. John of Avila preach in Granada. His public penance was so extreme that he was locked in an asylum, where he saw how cruelly the mentally ill were treated.

On his release he opened a hospital for the poor and sick and served them himself. His followers became the Brothers Hospitallers. He is a patron of hospitals, nurses, and the sick.
s198.intercession: St. John of God, pray for us. Bless all who care for the sick and the mentally ill, and give us compassion for every person who suffers. Amen.

s199.content:
Michele Ghislieri was a Dominican friar who became pope in 1566. He put the reforms of the Council of Trent into practice, issuing the Roman Catechism, a reformed Breviary, and the Roman Missal that would be used for four centuries.

He lived austerely, wore his white Dominican habit (the origin of the pope’s white cassock), and called all of Christendom to pray the Rosary before the naval Battle of Lepanto in 1571.
s199.intercession: Pope St. Pius V, pray for us. Strengthen the Church in faithful reform, and help us to turn to Our Lady’s Rosary in every trial. Amen.

s200.content:
Stanislaus was a Polish nobleman’s son studying in Vienna, where his brother bullied him for his piety. When his father forbade him to become a Jesuit, he set out on foot, walking hundreds of miles to St. Peter Canisius in Germany and then on to Rome, where St. Francis Borgia accepted him.

He entered the novitiate at seventeen and died of a fever nine months later, on the Feast of the Assumption. He is a patron of students, novices, and young people.
s200.intercession: St. Stanislaus, pray for us. Help young people to follow God’s call with determination, even when others do not understand. Amen.
